scope: Administrator-visible invitations with existing encryption; deletion of unused invitations and retention of used records

browser.create: code in existing table, no one-time modal
browser.copy: clipboard matches before and after refresh/restart
browser.persistence: original key and database restore displayed code
browser.revoke: unused row disappears and code cannot register
browser.used: record retained, no revoke action, backend deletion rejected

securityCases: SHA-256 lookup unchanged; display copy stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext with invitation ID associated data
Creation and list are administrator-only and no-store; hashes and ciphertext excluded from JSON
Used invitation deletion rejected on server; account and usage link retained
Physical deletion disables registration; no revoked-unused tombstone remains
Ten simultaneous consume/delete pairs permit exactly one success
Legacy hash-only invitation still registers; no code rotation
Swapped invitation ciphertext raises visible error without plaintext leakage
migration: migrateInvitationsV1 explicitly adds encrypted_code, preserving original hashes and fields; cleans only revoked unused rows. SQLite backup-copy fixture verifies repeated migration, used/revoked-used retention, untouched original database and old-model reads.
rollback: Previous image ignores added column; preserve original data and encryption key. Image-only rollback does not restore deleted invitations. Database snapshot restore requires review of restored invite usage/revocation state.
resolvedLocalFailures: Browser locator initially missed the existing Ant Design two-Chinese-character button spacing. Locator now matches the rendered label; same deletion assertions pass without application changes or skipped checks.
limitations: No deployment-server access or live-data migration performed
Legacy hashes cannot reveal their original code; existing code validity is retained
Migration backup-copy test uses SQLite; live MySQL/PostgreSQL upgrade was not exercised
